checks.name: central_question_resolved
checks.evidence: The question is whether they can free every odiyan, the queen's guard included, as the Thurai land. The book answers it. Ch 24: twenty-six of the thirty guards and most of the forty self-name at dusk, and Usha names herself to the queen. Ch 29: Chathu's forty pages turn out to be plain ink ('they never had any power'), and the Thurai withdraw and ask for a truce. Ch 30: the last unbound step forward; Lata names herself to Usha and Kamalakshi to Janu, and Neela says 'That's all of them.' Ch 31: the queen signs the charter ('No page, leaf or ledger of any member shall be held by the crown'), Sajan burns his own leaf, the other two remaining guard leaves are freed (their rolls cut off first) and Chathu's sheaf is burned. Ch 32: the fleet sails under an open truce. Only the Thurai rogue and the hire offer stay open. Caveat for the owner: Sajan never self-names, so by the book's own rule the queen is still a living witness who could write him again; his freedom rests on the charter, not the magic. Ch 24 also leaves eleven Resin House pages under Neela's hand with a promise to read them back at first light, and that hand-back is never shown. Both are minor continuity gaps, not an open book question.

checks.name: clues_paid_off
checks.evidence: All 23 outline clues are planted on the page and either pay off or are series threads. C01 (ch 7 to ch 16: 'A master who saw you turn can always write you again' snaps into place). C02 (ch 3 to ch 16: Kamalakshi's question is recalled). C03 (ch 13 grey-brown fingertips, ch 22 lamp-black smell, ch 29 'It's plain ink'). C04 (ch 2 folded bird in the thread, ch 16 'Spread for what the realm sees. Folded for what it needn't'). C05 (ch 2 'What did the naming cost?', ch 24 Usha names herself to the queen). C06 (ch 1 hitch, ch 7 Ponni and Ammini). C07 (ch 7 men in grey, ch 29 record laid out). C08 (ch 8 doubled-leaf coin, ch 29 'the same die'). C09 (ch 2 drill, ch 25 used, ch 28 'The killing strike is gone'). C10 (ch 5 to ch 27: Asha's last words given). C11 (ch 9 Muthu's warning, ch 12 Thankam and her paring knife, ch 26 Thankam's surgery). C14 (ch 4 'Ask me again', ch 11 the refugee escort written in the post book). C15 (ch 1 Pachan's map, ch 31 groves go to the Company 'under the map of Pachan'). C16 (ch 12 exact guard change, ch 16 'The day I gave you the landing count'). C17 (ch 13 'I am the last cage I hold', ch 29 'Written off. Paid in full. C.'). C18 (ch 10 corridor lamp, ch 27 'Keep the light there', ch 28 Janu's noon lamp). C19 (ch 12 Lata on petitions, paid off in ch 15 and ch 22, and the queen signs ch 31 in her own hand, 'no stamp'). C20 (ch 1 to ch 32: the boat named Kirri). C21 (ch 2 oilcloth writ, ch 30 read aloud and entered on the roll). C22 (ch 10 noon pricks, ch 19 the missed signal explained). C23 (ch 17 letter to Rema, ch 29 Rema at the gate). C12 and C13 are carried into ch 32 as series threads. No clue fails both tests.

checks.name: midpoint_reversal
checks.evidence: ch 16 (outline midpoint): the queen walks into the drying shed with a fresh page for Usha in tacky resin-ink: 'You carried away paper. You can't carry away what I saw.' The page theft is recast as a paper victory, Usha is shown to have informed her, the folded bird is owned as the queen's private hand, and Chathu's forty are set down: 'Your forty are mine too, whenever I choose.' The reversal changes the romance directly. The offer prices Devan's office ('I give Devan back Kettamala... Safe, unseen, and mine'). Neela withholds the noon signal from him to keep it from the queen. And she realises: 'The only freedom I have ever had is the one that bleeds when he does.' This sets up Devan's unilateral refusal in ch 17 and the breach he repairs in ch 20.

checks.name: heroine_belief_change
checks.evidence: The belief moves from 'Freedom means belonging to no one' to 'Freedom is choosing who I'm bound to.' Ch 28 is the proof: Neela writes her name first on the Company roll in daylight, binding herself to the Company's vote and making herself the crown's first name to answer. She says: 'For twenty-one years I answered to a number. I wanted to be no one's. I wanted it so much I called it freedom... It was a very quiet cage. Nobody in it ever bled for me.' She then writes 'Indu, called Neela, of Nellimala and Kettamala.' In ch 1 she chalks her name last, hopes nobody will notice she is in charge, and keeps her birth name small beside the other. Ch 24 sets this up when she refuses the command in public: 'It is not belonging to no one. It is choosing who you're tied to.'

checks.name: real_loss
checks.evidence: ch 27: Vellan dies holding Kamalakshi's carved bird: 'after a long time, when the breath had not come again, she put two fingers to the big man's throat... Then she took her hand away and shook her head.' He stays dead; ch 28 leaves a lamp-black smear for him on the plank. Ch 25 and ch 28: Devan's right hand is permanently lost. Thankam says 'The hand won't come back,' Devan answers 'Then it won't,' and ch 32 has him teaching a left-handed drill. Further losses that stay lost: Biju (ch 8), Sankaran, Chami and Rajan (ch 11), and Lekha, Orma, Kani, Swathi and Sreedhar on Kandan's tile (ch 27).

checks.name: love_interest_goal
checks.evidence: ch 1 to ch 2: Devan's goal is to hold the Monkey Pass for the villages behind it, without office and without the crown's leave. In ch 1 he says 'I mean to go down and hold the gorge.' In ch 2, after reading 'as they always have', 'His goal... went hard as set mortar. He held the Monkey Pass.' He pursues it through ch 5, ch 8, ch 11, ch 14, ch 19 and ch 23 to ch 25. In ch 3 it puts him on the opposite side of Neela's Kodiyur vote, so it is independent of her.

checks.name: series_hinge
checks.evidence: ch 32: a Thurai envoy under truce cloth comes to hire the Night Company. Beside him walks a scarred odiyan whose wrists smell of 'Salt. Sweet, dry clove-bark, and under that the bitter scorch of resin.' Neela: 'He was in none of it.' The envoy says he 'is in no book you hold.' Neela concludes 'Someone had been making odiyans in a place she had not found, and the sea lords had him on a leash of salt.' Koman also reports the long river shape watching the road. The book's own question is closed before the hinge opens, and the chapter ends on the Company's first vote: 'We vote at noon.'

series_threads.thread: Salt-and-clove-bark resin on scarred Thurai wrists. Planted ch 6 (sleeper by the tower), echoed ch 8 (dead scout). It becomes the book-two hinge in ch 32: a rogue odiyan in no ledger arrives with the Thurai envoy, implying another maker of odiyans across the sea.

A long, low river shape no Company scent matches. Planted ch 17, it returns in ch 20 (it watches the shelf and takes nothing), ch 26 (it pulls Thurai wounded from the river and does not fight) and ch 32 (it watches the reopened road). Its nature and allegiance are left open for book two.

summary: The book passes all seven checks. The central question closes in ch 29 to ch 31 through the plain-ink reveal, the last self-namings and the signed charter. Every outline clue is planted and paid off, except C12 and C13, which are carried into the ch 32 hinge as series threads. The ch 16 midpoint recasts the first half and prices Devan's fort against Neela's answer, which drives the ch 17 breach and the ch 20 repair. Neela's belief change is proven by the ch 28 daylight signing. Vellan's death and Devan's lost hand stay lost. Devan's pass goal is independent of the heroine. The ch 32 hinge opens a bigger question without leaving the book's own open. Continuity notes for the owner, none blocking: (1) Sajan never self-names, so under the book's witness rule the queen could still write him again; his freedom rests on the charter alone, and one line acknowledging this would close it. (2) In ch 24 Neela holds eleven members' Resin House pages and promises to read them back at first light, but the hand-back is never shown, and holding them sits awkwardly with the ch 3 rule that a page held by its subject cannot be read against her. (3) Two loose threads outside the clue list: the fresh yellow bird on the Thurai supply cart in ch 17 implies current crown supply but is never explained, and the grey steward's 'Has she come?' in ch 13 is never followed up. (4) Small count and detail drifts: forty-two versus forty-three people in ch 1 to ch 4, the tangled page arithmetic in ch 24, and Pavi's crooked left hand described differently in ch 20.
